nodes.statement:
The HRA reference-organs endpoint returns 81 real organ entries
across 58 distinct organ slugs, 69/81 (85.2%) resolving to a
UBERON-prefixed CURIE, split 45 female-specific / 36 male-specific --
confirming the Step-based fetch drives a complete, ontology-keyed
whole-organ scaffold that downstream biomodel annotation and the 3D
crosswalk both key off of.

nodes.statement:
The HRA cell-type-term-occurences endpoint returns 149 distinct Cell
Ontology (CL) terms, count-sorted; the top term (CL:0000000) occurs
2,762 times, an order of magnitude above an 8-term tier that clusters
at exactly 266 occurrences each -- consistent with those terms
co-occurring as a fixed per-record annotation bundle in whatever HRA
datasets contribute them.

BioModels t...
nodes.statement:
Synonym-based organ tagging matched 5/25 (20%) glucose-regulation
BioModels to an HRA organ, correctly concentrating on pancreas (4
models -- Topp beta-cell-mass, Silber IV-glucose, Sturis and Tolic
insulin-glucose oscillators) and liver (1 model, Bulik2016 hepatic
glucose metabolism) -- exactly the two organs glucose-homeostasis
biology predicts (insulin/glucagon secretion + hepatic glucose
buffering), confirming the synonym-match mechanism assigns organs
correctly when it fires.

nodes.statement:
Of the 168 CVTerm hits behind the annotation catalog's 114 organ-tagged
models, 156 (92.9%) resolve through the curated BTO->organ crosswalk
and only 12 (7.1%) through a direct Uberon/FMA MIRIAM match --
BTO-via-crosswalk is the dominant, not incidental, organ-matching
mechanism, and `BQB_OCCURS_IN`/`BQB_IS` are the dominant qualifiers
(88 and 40 of 168 hits).

nodes.label:
Annotation-based organ matching reaches 114/1,096 models (10.4%,
14 organs) v...
nodes.statement:
Annotation-based organ matching reaches 114/1,096 models (10.4%,
14 organs) vs name-only matching's 82/1,096 (7.5%, 10 organs) over
the same 1,096-model corpus, adding 85 models and 4 whole organs
(lymph-node, ovary, spleen, urinary-bladder) the name matcher cannot
reach because those organ names never appear verbatim in a BioModels
title -- confirming annotation-based matching is a materially
higher-recall complement to, not merely a duplicate of, name-synonym
matching.

nodes.label:
All 1,096 curated BioModels harvest into one JSON DB with dense
molecular cov...
nodes.statement:
All 1,096 curated BioModels harvest into one JSON DB with dense
molecular coverage and recall-limited-but-real HRA-anatomy coverage.
Molecular (from the models' own SBML/BioPAX): GO 967 (88%), UniProt
507 (46%), CHEBI 480 (44%), KEGG 322 (29%); 978 models (89%) carry
>=1 molecular id. The DB also resolves organism for 684 models (62%)
and gene ids from UniProt — HGNC 302 (28%), Ensembl 360 (33%). HRA
anatomy (reconstructed via SBML Uberon/CL + BTO->Uberon +
paper-MeSH->Uberon/CL crosswalks + a new ASCT+B gene->Uberon lever):
Uberon 323 (29%), cell types 363 (33%), organs 264 (24%), FTUs 163
(15%) — the gene lever lifting each over the paper-MeSH-only baseline
(Uberon 215, organs 180, cell types 322, FTUs 116). HRApop measured
cell-type populations attach to 112 models (10%).

nodes.label:
The molecular-vs-anatomy coverage gap (89% molecular vs 29% Uberon)
reflects ...
nodes.statement:
The molecular-vs-anatomy coverage gap (89% molecular vs 29% Uberon)
reflects BioModels curation practice: models are annotated for
biochemistry (species -> CHEBI/UniProt/KEGG, reactions -> GO), not for
anatomy, so HRA mapping depends on reconstructing anatomical context
from outside the model — the paper's PubMed MeSH headings (reaching
915 models, 83%) and, newly, the model's own genes via the ASCT+B
gene->Uberon crosswalk are the two anatomy levers. The gene lever
narrowed the gap (Uberon 20% -> 29%), but anatomy still trails the
dense molecular annotation because most models carry no anatomy in
their own SBML.

nodes.label:
The baseline (build_if_missing: false) loads the committed
datasets/model_hra...
nodes.statement:
The baseline (build_if_missing: false) loads the committed
datasets/model_hra_map.json network-free through the two-source
registry and reports it exactly as stored: 1,576 models -- 1,096
repository=biomodels + 480 repository=physionet, now that the
PhysioNet harvest has run against the committed DB. The BioModels-only
coverage stats are unchanged from biomodel-hra-map's
(n_with_molecular=978, n_with_hrapop=112), confirming PhysioNet rows
carry no molecular/HRApop annotations of their own; n_with_uberon rose
from 323 (BioModels alone) to 447 (323 BioModels + 124 PhysioNet,
offline keyword-mapped), showing the ModelHarvestStep's load path is a
pure superset wrapper over the existing BioModels DB plus the
newly-upserted PhysioNet rows, not a reinterpretation of either.

nodes.label:
The harvest is source-registry-driven and identifier-keyed, so it is
structur...
nodes.statement:
The harvest is source-registry-driven and identifier-keyed, so it is
structurally incremental and non-destructive: should_process skips
anything already in the DB (a plain rerun only fetches newly-posted
models), and each source's entry_fn only ever upserts its own rows
under its own identifier scheme (BioModels IRIs vs. PhysioNet content
URLs), so a PhysioNet refresh cannot touch a BioModels row and vice
versa. That is what lets this one study stand in for "refresh the
whole unified DB" rather than needing a separate study per source.
